name: EAGLE-2: Faster Inference of Language Models with Dynamic Draft Trees
problem: Static draft trees (as in EAGLE-1, SpecInfer) implicitly assume a draft token's acceptance rate depends only on its POSITION in the tree, which is false.
mechanism: Context-AWARE dynamic draft tree. Uses EAGLE's observation that the draft model's confidence scores approximate acceptance rates with small error (i.e. the draft model is well-calibrated) to expand the draft tree at each step according to the draft model's own confidences rather than a fixed topology: expand the highest-confidence node, allocate tree nodes by predicted acceptance rate, and prune low-value branches. Reranking of the verified candidates also uses the draft confidence. Output distribution provably unchanged - lossless.
speedup_reported: 3.05x-4.26x speedup, which is 20%-40% faster than EAGLE-1, across three LLM series and six tasks. Model pairs follow EAGLE-1 (Vicuna/LLaMA2-Chat family, feature-level draft head). The 20-40% figure is the like-for-like delta against EAGLE-1 on the same backbone, which is the more honest comparison than the 3.05-4.26x against vanilla decoding.
notes: ADOPTION: EAGLE-2 is reachable in vLLM and SGLang, and the EAGLE-3 follow-up (pap-eff-eagle-3) is what engines actually default to, so EAGLE-2 is best described as shipped-but-superseded rather than actively preferred. VENUE NOTE: no venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar, arXiv comment empty, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = arXiv v1 (Jun 2024). IMPORTANT REPRODUCTION CAVEAT, stated by the authors themselves: this paper's premise is that acceptance rate is context-dependent. Any reimplementation that reuses a static tree from EAGLE-1 while citing EAGLE-2's numbers has not implemented EAGLE-2. The claimed gain is a change of tree TOPOLOGY per input, not a cheaper verify kernel - so the speedup will not transfer across models whose confidence distributions differ from the tested ones.
